intro: An Austin punk band on the eve of a label deal.
story: A Giant Dog are an Austin punk band who tore up Pickathon in 2015, just before they signed to Merge Records. They have grown from scrappy garage-punk into theatrical glam-rock, with the concept album Bite in 2023. In November 2026 co-founder Andrew Cashen gave an Austin songwriting talk about his work with the band and with Sweet Spirit.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 4 pm, Mountain Stage · Sun Aug 2, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A bluegrass and old-time pioneer.
story: Alice Gerrard has been singing since the 1960s, and was already a pioneer of bluegrass and old-time music when she played Pickathon in 2015. She was inducted into the IBMA Hall of Fame in 2017, with Hazel Dickens, and published her memoir Custom Made Woman in 2025. In March 2026 she was the centerpiece of a Knoxville celebration of women in old-time music.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 11:10 am, Meadow Stage · Sun Aug 2, 5:20 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: An Oklahoma garage-pop band, loose and melodic.
story: BRONCHO are a garage-pop band from Norman, Oklahoma who played Pickathon in 2015 with loose, melodic songs. Double Vanity followed in 2016. After seven years without a record they returned in 2025 with Natural Pleasure, on Kung Fu Records, in a hazier, shoegaze-leaning mood.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 5:10 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: A young flatpicker from Michigan, as a duo with Don Julin.
story: Billy Strings was a young bluegrass flatpicker from Michigan who played Pickathon in 2015 as a duo with Don Julin, and came back in 2017. The IBMA gave him its Momentum Award in 2016, and Home, on Rounder in 2019, won the Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album in 2021. Live Vol. 1 won again in 2025, and Highway Prayers in 2026.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 6:40 pm, Lucky Barn · Sat Aug 1, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Dylan Baldi's noisy Cleveland indie rock.
story: Cloud Nothings are Dylan Baldi's Cleveland band, already respected for raw, noisy indie rock after Attack on Memory in 2012 and Here and Nowhere Else in 2014, when they played Pickathon in 2015. Life Without Sound came in 2017 and The Shadow I Remember in 2021. In 2026 they announced a 2027 North American tour ahead of What Kind of Hell Did You Survive? on Pure Noise.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 8:40 pm, Mountain Stage · Mon Aug 3, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A Brooklyn dream-pop band on the rise.
story: DIIV were a fast-rising Brooklyn group of dreamy, guitar-driven indie rock, after Oshin on Captured Tracks in 2012, when they played Pickathon in 2015. Is the Is Are followed in 2016 and Deceiver in 2019, then Frog in Boiling Water in 2024. ZIRP!, produced by A. G. Cook, came out on Fantasy in 2026, and they toured North America with Interpol.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 9:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An old-time string-band torchbearer.
story: Dom Flemons was already a celebrated torchbearer of old-time string-band music when he played Pickathon in 2015. Black Cowboys, on Smithsonian Folkways, followed in 2018, and the Living Blues critics' poll honored him in 2019. Traveling Wildfire came in 2023, and in 2026 he announced an album recorded on historic instruments from the Smithsonian's collections.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 3:40 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 2, 12:30 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: A Portland singer of borderless Latin folk.
story: Edna Vazquez is a Portland singer whose rich voice and borderless Latin folk songs made her a hometown favorite at Pickathon in 2015. She continues to record solo, with Te Esperaba on Estereo Heinz Records, and to perform with Pink Martini.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 3:30 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 2, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A guitarist from the beginning of ska and reggae.
story: Ernest Ranglin was already a towering figure in ska and reggae guitar when he played Pickathon in 2015. At 93 he has largely stepped back from live performance, and he has spoken to Guitar World about a career of more than seven decades.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 2:50 pm, Meadow Stage · Sun Aug 2, 6:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Mary Timony's Washington power trio.
story: Ex Hex are Mary Timony's Washington, D.C. power trio, whose sharp hooks and twin-guitar swagger arrived at Pickathon in 2015, a year after Rips on Merge. It's Real came in 2019, followed by a few East Coast club shows in late 2023.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 12:20 pm, Mountain Stage · Sun Aug 2, 7 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: Louisville alt-country pioneers with dark harmonies.
story: Freakwater are the Louisville alt-country duo of Catherine Irwin and Janet Bean, whose dark harmonies have run since 1989 and whose Old Paint came out on Thrill Jockey in 1995. They played Pickathon in 2005 and again in 2015, and still surface on their own terms, as at a Louisville show in June 2026.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 5:50 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 4 pm, Mountain Stage

intro: Eric D. Johnson's folk-rock band, on its third visit.
story: Fruit Bats is Eric D. Johnson's band, and they had played Pickathon in 2010 and 2011 before they came back in 2015. Absolute Loser followed in 2016 on Easy Sound and Gold Past Life in 2019 on Merge, and they returned again in 2016, 2019 and 2025. The Landfill came out on Merge in June 2026.

intro: Howe Gelb's desert-rock band.
story: Giant Sand is Howe Gelb's Tucson band, which has been making desert rock since 1980 and came to Pickathon in 2015. Gelb marked his seventieth birthday with an expanded Giant Giant Sand lineup in a hometown celebration at La Rosa.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 1, 8:40 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: A Portland psychedelic indie-rock band.
story: Grandparents are a Portland psychedelic indie-rock band who played Pickathon in 2015 as a homegrown favorite. Public records of the band end around 2016.
sets: Thu Jul 30, 9:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Jul 31, 3:30 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: A London trio of warm, off-kilter indie rock.
story: Happyness are a London trio of warm, off-kilter indie rock, who played Pickathon in 2015, the year after Weird Little Birthday. Write In came in 2017 and Floatr, their last major studio album, in 2020.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 5:10 pm, Lucky Barn · Sat Aug 1, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: Erika Wennerstrom's powerhouse band, back for a third visit.
story: Heartless Bastards are Erika Wennerstrom's band, who played Pickathon in 2010 and 2012 before they came back in 2015. A Beautiful Life came out in 2021 on Sweet Unknown Records. Wennerstrom, now in Austin, launched a twentieth-anniversary tour of All This Time across the Midwest and Texas.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 9:20 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: M.C. Taylor's soul-leaning folk band, back for a second visit.
story: Hiss Golden Messenger is M.C. Taylor's band, and they played Pickathon in 2014 and returned in 2015, a year after Lateness of Dancers on Merge. Terms of Surrender, from 2019, was nominated for the Grammy for Best Americana Album in 2021. I'm People followed in 2026 on Chrysalis.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 10:50 pm, Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 2, 1 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Texas Hill Country songwriter of pedal-steel Americana.
story: Israel Nash is a songwriter from the Texas Hill Country whose expansive, pedal-steel-drenched Americana was catching fire when he played Pickathon in 2015. Lifted came in 2018 and Ozarker on Loose in 2023, and he revisited his breakthrough with a deluxe edition of Israel Nash's Rain Plans, with rare demos and rooftop live takes.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 11 pm, Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 2, 8:40 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: A vintage rock-and-roll singer from Oklahoma, back after 2013.
story: JD McPherson is an Oklahoma singer and guitarist whose crisp rock-and-roll and R&B drew an Americana Music Association emerging-act nomination in 2013, the year he first came to Pickathon. He returned in 2015, the year of Let the Good Times Roll on Rounder. Undivided Heart & Soul followed on New West in 2017, and in March 2026 he scored a film, The Lowdown.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 5 pm, Mountain Stage · Sun Aug 2, 4:20 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland psych-folk songwriter.
story: Jackson Boone is a Portland psych-folk songwriter who was a local fixture at Pickathon in 2015. His last documented releases and hometown appearances date to 2018 and 2019.
sets: Thu Jul 30, 2:40 pm, Treeline Stage · Fri Jul 31, 2:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A solo guitarist with a mysterious, otherworldly voice.
story: Jessica Pratt played Pickathon in 2013 and returned in 2015, the year of On Your Own Love Again on Drag City, after her self-titled 2012 debut. Quiet Signs followed on Mexican Summer in 2019, and Here in the Pitch in 2024 drew praise across the year-end lists. In 2025 she played festival and theater dates in Europe and California.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 6:50 pm, Treeline Stage · Sat Aug 1, 11:20 am, Woods Stage

intro: A Kentucky songwriter of quiet, luminous folk.
story: Joan Shelley is a Kentucky songwriter whose quiet, luminous folk songs made her a treasured Pickathon visitor in 2015, the year of Over and Even on No Quarter. Joan Shelley followed in 2017, then Like the River Loves the Sea in 2019. She recorded Real Warmth in Toronto with producer Ben Whiteley and toured through 2026.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 5:10 pm, Meadow Stage · Sat Aug 1, 2:10 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Three Oregon sisters with blood harmonies.
story: Joseph are three sisters from the Pacific Northwest whose blood harmonies made them a standout at Pickathon in 2015, and they came back in 2016. After Allison Closner stepped away, Natalie and Meegan Closner carried on as a duo, releasing Closer to Happy and scheduling tenth-anniversary shows.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 3:40 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: A cosmic spiritual-jazz saxophonist, just reaching beyond jazz.
story: Kamasi Washington arrived at Pickathon in 2015, the year The Epic came out on Brainfeeder and began carrying his spiritual jazz to listeners well beyond the jazz world. Heaven and Earth followed in 2018. He became a festival regular and a film composer, with a 2020 Emmy nomination for the score to Becoming, and in fall 2026 he toured North America.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 6:20 pm, Mountain Stage · Fri Jul 31, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A songwriter stepping into his own.
story: Kevin Morby was just stepping into his own as a solo songwriter when he played Pickathon in 2015, and he came back in 2016, the year of Singing Saw on Dead Oceans. City Music followed in 2017, Oh My God in 2019 and Sundowner in 2020. Little Wide Open, produced by Aaron Dessner, came in 2026, with a world tour.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 1:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 11:20 am, Woods Stage

intro: Kyle Thomas's fuzzy glam-garage anthems, back after 2013.
story: King Tuff is Kyle Thomas, whose fuzzy, hook-filled glam-garage anthems came to Pickathon in 2013 and again in 2015, the year after Black Moon Spell on Sub Pop. The Other came in 2018 and Smalltown Stardust in 2023, in gentler psych-folk textures. In late 2026 he scheduled club dates with Sheer Mag.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 1 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 10 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A heart-on-sleeve folk-rock songwriter, here for his fifth visit.
story: Langhorne Slim came to Pickathon in 2007 as a young songwriter on the rise and returned in 2008, 2010, 2012 and 2015, a long run of high-energy, heart-on-sleeve folk-rock after his 2008 self-titled album on Kemado. He remains a tireless live performer, with holiday dates in late 2026 and a 2027 tour supporting Grace Potter.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 6:20 pm, Mountain Stage

intro: A Texas soul singer right before liftoff.
story: Leon Bridges played Pickathon in 2015, the year Coming Home came out on Columbia, and the Americana Music Association nominated him as an emerging act in 2016. Good Thing followed in 2018, Gold-Diggers Sound in 2021 and Leon in 2024. His fifth album, Happiness Anytime, was co-produced with members of Jungle, and he launched international tour dates.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 8 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 8:50 pm, Mountain Stage

intro: A New Orleans juke-joint bluesman.
story: Little Freddie King is a New Orleans bluesman of unvarnished juke-joint style who has played since 1972 and visited Pickathon in 2015. Still going strong in his mid-eighties, he appeared in Spinal Tap II and released the live album Live at BJ's Lounge on MadeWright Records.
sets: Sun Aug 2, 10 am, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 5 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A Portland gospel and soul voice.
story: Liz Vice is a Portland-born singer whose church-rooted soul voice made her a standout at Pickathon in 2015. She has kept sharing groove-driven R&B and gospel songs on her own terms, and recently released the single The Call.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 8:30 pm, Treeline Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:20 am, Mountain Stage

intro: A North Carolina duo, here for the second of five visits.
story: Mandolin Orange are Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz, whose close harmonies won listeners over at Pickathon in 2014, and they returned in 2015, the year of Such Jubilee. They came back in 2017, 2019 and 2023, and renamed themselves Watchhouse in 2021. Rituals came out on Thirty Tigers in 2025.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 2:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:40 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Los Angeles garage-psych band.
story: Meatbodies are Chad Ubovich's Los Angeles fuzz-rock band, who played Pickathon for the first time in 2015, a year after their self-titled album on In the Red, with loud, tangled garage-psych. Alice came in 2017 and Flora Ocean Tiger Bloom, long in the making, in 2024. They returned to the farm in 2017 and 2026.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 9:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 1, 2:40 pm, Mountain Stage

intro: A Durham banjo player pushing old-time into new shapes.
story: Nathan Bowles is a banjoist and percussionist from Durham, North Carolina, who played Pickathon in 2015 as an adventurous player of Appalachian traditions. Plainly Mistaken came in 2018. He pushes old-time music into hypnotic shapes with tape loops and ensembles, and returned to Pickathon in 2026 with solo sets of banjo, tape loops and keyboards.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 1:50 pm, Treeline Stage · Sat Aug 1, 12:40 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A one-off gathering of Tar Heel State roots musicians.
story: The North Carolina All Stars were a one-time showcase of roots musicians from the Tar Heel State, billed together at Pickathon in 2015. The name was a festival billing, not a touring band, and there is no recent news.

intro: A Brazilian songwriter, before Narcos.
story: Rodrigo Amarante was already revered in Brazil for Los Hermanos and for his solo debut Cavalo, from 2013, when he played Pickathon in 2015. Soon after, his Narcos theme Tuyo reached millions, and Drama followed on Polyvinyl in 2021. Now in Los Angeles, he is writing a new album due in 2027.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 4:10 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 1, 1:30 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: A fiery acoustic guitarist from Illinois.
story: Ryley Walker played Pickathon in 2015, the year of Primrose Green on Dead Oceans, with fiery acoustic guitar work rooted in British and American folk. Golden Sings That Have Been Sung came in 2016, Deafman Glance in 2018 and Course in Fable in 2021. He has since turned toward computer-based electronic production, as with the single Carrier on the London label AD 93.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 7:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 1, 3:50 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: A playful reinventor of traditional ballads, back in 2018.
story: Sam Amidon was a favorite at Pickathon in 2015 for his playful, left-field reinventions of traditional ballads, two years after Bright Sunny South on Nonesuch, and he returned in 2018. Salt River came on River Lea in 2025, and Willing Brother Knowing, produced by Big Thief's James Krivchenia, is due in February 2027.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 12:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 1, 5:10 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A Brooklyn songwriter and producer, out of Yellowbirds.
story: Sam Cohen came to Pickathon in 2015 with warm psychedelic pop songs, fresh from years in the band Yellowbirds. He has since become a sought-after producer, for artists including Kevin Morby, and released the ambient instrumental album Slow Fawn Music No. 1 on 30th Century Records.
sets: Thu Jul 30, 11 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Jul 31, 1:40 pm, Mountain Stage

intro: Ishmael Butler's cosmic Seattle hip-hop, back after 2013.
story: Shabazz Palaces are Ishmael Butler's Seattle collective, whose cosmic, boundary-pushing hip-hop came to Pickathon in 2013 and again in 2015, the year after Lese Majesty on Sub Pop. Quazarz came in 2017 and The Don of Diamond Dreams in 2020. Their eighth album, It's A Style Sport, came out on Sub Pop in October 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 1, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage · Sat Aug 1, 8:40 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: Ahmed Gallab's Sudanese pop, funk and krautrock.
story: Sinkane is Ahmed Gallab's project of Sudanese pop, funk and krautrock, which came to Pickathon in 2015, the year after Mean Love on DFA. Life & Livin' It followed in 2017 on City Slang. In 2026 Gallab announced He's Gone, due in February 2027 on City Slang, with a single featuring Mdou Moctar.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 6:10 pm, Meadow Stage · Sun Aug 2, 6:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Sonny Smith's sun-bleached San Francisco garage-pop.
story: Sonny & the Sunsets is Sonny Smith's wry, sun-bleached San Francisco garage-pop band, who played Pickathon in 2011, 2012 and 2015. Smith works between music, plays and visual art, and in 2026 the band played California festival and club dates after a fall 2025 tour of the U.S. West Coast and Australia.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Mon Aug 3, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage

intro: A scrappy Portland indie-rock band.
story: Summer Cannibals are a Portland indie-rock band led by Jessica Boudreaux, who played Pickathon in 2015. After several years' hiatus, she reunited the band to open for L7 in Portland, and has been recording new music.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 4:40 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 2 pm, Treeline Stage

intro: A rowdy Bay Area string band.
story: The Brothers Comatose are a Bay Area string band of rowdy, good-time acoustic music who played Pickathon in 2015 and returned in 2026. They remain a road-tested favorite of the Americana circuit, and put out Golden Grass in 2025.
sets: Fri Jul 31, late night (12:40 am), Galaxy Barn · Fri Jul 31, 7:30 pm, Meadow Stage · Sun Aug 2, 3:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A California country duo.
story: The Easy Leaves are a Northern California country duo who played Pickathon in 2015, and again in 2016, with honky-tonk harmonies. Their public performances taper off around 2020.
sets: Thu Jul 30, 4:20 pm, Treeline Stage · Fri Jul 31, 12:30 pm, Meadow Stage

intro: A Texas Western swing trio with three fiddles.
story: The Quebe Sisters are a Texas Western swing trio, already known for triple fiddles and tight harmonies when they played Pickathon in 2015. They announced an open-ended hiatus after a farewell tour in 2023.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 5:20 pm, Treeline Stage · Sun Aug 2, 2 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Tamara Lindeman's spare, observant folk.
story: The Weather Station is Tamara Lindeman's project, spare and observant when it played Pickathon in 2015, the year of Loyalty on Paradise of Bachelors, a Polaris Prize long-list album. The band grew into a lush, jazz-inflected art-rock ensemble: Ignorance came in 2021 and Humanhood in 2025, a Polaris long-list record that drew a 2026 Juno nomination for Adult Alternative Album of the Year.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 3:40 pm, Treeline Stage · Sun Aug 2, 12:30 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A virtuoso six-string bassist with cosmic humor.
story: Thundercat played Pickathon in 2015, two years after Apocalypse on Brainfeeder, with a virtuosic six-string bass and cosmic humor. A Grammy for These Walls, with Kendrick Lamar, followed in 2016, and It Is What It Is won the Grammy for Best Progressive R&B Album in 2021. Distracted, his 2026 album, brought a North American tour.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: The desert blues of the Sahara.
story: Tinariwen are a Malian Tuareg collective whose hypnotic desert blues, heard on Tassili, won the Grammy for Best World Music Album in 2012, and who played Pickathon in 2015 and again in 2018. Elwan came in 2017 and Amadjar in 2019. Hoggar, on Wedge in 2026, was followed by tours of Europe and South America.
sets: Sun Aug 2, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 2, 9:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Cleveland indie-pop band of scruffy guitars.
story: Total Babes are a Cleveland indie-pop band of scruffy, hook-filled guitars who played Pickathon in 2015 around their album Heydays. There is no recent news.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 2 pm, Treeline Stage · Sun Aug 2, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Merrill Garbus's looping, polyrhythmic pop.
story: Tune-Yards is Merrill Garbus, whose looping vocals and polyrhythmic percussion were a highlight of Pickathon in 2015, after w h o k i l l in 2011 and Nikki Nack in 2014, both on 4AD. She now works as a duo with Nate Brenner. Better Dreaming came in 2025, followed by the EP Tell the Future With Your Body.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 9:50 pm, Mountain Stage · Sun Aug 2, 7:40 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A literary Oklahoma country band.
story: Turnpike Troubadours were beloved across Texas and Oklahoma for literary, hard-charging country when they played Pickathon in 2015, a year after their self-titled album on Bossier City. They went on hiatus and came back in 2022, with A Cat in the Rain in 2023, The Price of Admission, produced by Shooter Jennings, in 2025, and the Americana Association's Duo/Group of the Year nomination in 2024 and 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 7:20 pm, Mountain Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:20 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A garage-rock dynamo, here with the Roling Stons.
story: Ty Segall played Pickathon in 2013, 2015, 2016 and 2017, and in 2015 his set was billed Ty Segall and the Roling Stons. He kept recording steadily: Freedom's Goblin in 2018, First Taste in 2019, Possession in 2025 and Chrome in 2026, with the companion EP Love Fuzzz and a South American tour in November 2026.

intro: Andy Cabic's California indie-folk project.
story: Vetiver is Andy Cabic's California folk-rock project, which played Pickathon in 2009, 2011 and 2015, after Tight Knit in 2009 and The Errant Charm in 2011, both on Sub Pop. It grew into a mellow, groove-oriented outfit, and there is no recent news.

intro: A Calgary post-punk quartet, soon to be Preoccupations.
story: Viet Cong were a Calgary quartet whose taut, angular post-punk was turning heads when they played Pickathon in 2015, the year their self-titled album came out on Jagjaguwar. They renamed themselves Preoccupations in 2016 and stayed committed to a dark, driving sound, releasing Ill At Ease and touring Europe and North America.

intro: Cory Hanson's heavy, shape-shifting garage-psych.
story: Wand are Cory Hanson's Los Angeles group, whose heavy, shape-shifting garage-psych came to Pickathon in 2015, and they returned in 2018. They have grown from scuzzy volume into intricate, orchestral-tinged rock, and toured behind Vertigo on Drag City, with SXSW showcases and West Coast dates into 2026.

intro: A Michigan honky-tonker with Waylon in his bones.
story: Whitey Morgan is a Michigan honky-tonker whose Waylon-indebted country came to Pickathon in 2011 and returned in 2012 and 2015. True to his blue-collar approach, he has stayed on the road, booking club dates across North America through late 2026 and early 2027.

intro: A Nashville instrumental guitarist.
story: William Tyler is a Nashville guitarist of reflective, fingerpicked compositions who played Pickathon in 2015, two years after Impossible Truth on Merge. He returned in 2017 with his Modern Country Band, after Modern Country in 2016. Goes West came in 2019, and Time Indefinite in 2025.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 5:10 pm, Treeline Stage · Sat Aug 1, 6:40 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A British folk-psych quartet of heavy, pastoral riffs.
story: Wolf People are a British folk-psych quartet whose heavy, pastoral riffs came to Pickathon in 2015 and again in 2017, after Ruins in 2016. They announced an indefinite hiatus in January 2020.
